feature: Villagers made from the player model
description: Villagers are built from the player model with vanilla clothes, tools and hair.

feature: Names and looks from a seed
description: Each villager gets a fixed name and look from a stored seed, so he looks the same every time he loads.
Skin tones come from the darker three quarters of the slider and some hair styles are left out per gender.
Villagers are slightly see-through with a faint teal tint and a soft glow after dark, as echoes in the afterlife.
source: ROADMAP M6; 2026-11-06 notes S6 to S10; GhostLook.cs
notes: Tyler approved it subtle, villagers only, no particles or lights. Tuning paused at his request; GhostAlpha has little effect with the borrowed shader.

description: Villagers are neutral to players, fight monsters, and only turn on you if you attack them.
A setting sets how much health villagers have.

feature: Nothing drops when a villager dies
description: A dead villager drops none of his gear or tools.
A newly founded village starts with a couple of settlers at the hearth.

feature: Newcomers only for a free bed
description: A newcomer only arrives when there is an empty bed, by day, walking in from the edge of the village.
notes: Replaces the old rule of new villagers every few days.

description: Each villager household gets its own small house; small homes hold one bed, larger homes two.
Each villager claims a bed and sleeps from a bedtime between 22:00 and 23:00 to a wake time between 05:00 and 06:00.
notes: Lying down tested without stutter; the fix that counts beds inside designs is not tested yet.

feature: Rest under a roof without a bed
description: A villager with no bed rests at his own spot under a roof.

feature: Cook real food at the hearth
description: Villagers put raw meat on the hearth's cooking station, wait its cooking time, take it off and keep the meal in the chest.
A hurt villager eats cooked food and heals by the food's own regen, like a player.
notes: The first version (kneel at the hearth and heal) was tested and then replaced by real cooking.

feature: Roasted scraps when there is no food
description: With no food at all a hurt villager heals slowly from roasted scraps.
A village with no cooking station makes one before anything else so it can heal.
Each villager has a mood from needs and fading thoughts (slept well, hurt, ate well), scaled by his voice.
source: ROADMAP M4; Moods.cs; MineColonies; Hirdmandr; Millénaire

description: The village has a mood from its people and its state, shown on the hearth.
When a villager dies it goes in the chronicle and the whole village is sad for about a day.
A couple with a home, food and a free bed may have a child, who grows up over four days and does not work.
source: ROADMAP M6; Childhood.cs; Millénaire; MCA Reborn

description: Villagers who have lived 40 days in the village become elders who do lighter work and tell the village's story.
source: LIVING_WORLD_RESEARCH #18; WORLD_LIFE round 2; Elders.cs; Banished; MCA

description: From day 60 an elder may die peacefully in the night and be mourned.
notes: Needs WorldLife on.

description: Elders walk and work more slowly as they age.
A child takes one parent's homeland and the other's pastime.
A child's face, hair and skin come from its parents.
Children take some of their parents' traits.
A villager missing a bed, food or safety grumbles after 3 days, asks a player after 6 and leaves after 10.

feature: Request on the notice board at the demand stage
description: A villager's unmet need is also posted on the notice board when he starts to demand it.

feature: Villagers leave and move to a neighbour
description: An unhappy villager says goodbye and walks to the neighbour village his village likes best, and turns up there as a newcomer.
notes: Needs WorldLife on. Nobody leaves a village of two, nor the Jarl.

description: A small hamlet is content with little; a grown village wants a longhouse, seats, a fence and varied food.
source: LIVING_WORLD_RESEARCH #2; Expectations.cs; RimWorld; Songs of Syx

description: Villagers are happier when they have eaten several different foods in the last three days.
Friends claim beds near each other and rivals far apart; living next to a rival sours the mood.
Two single friends move into a two-bed home together and may have children.
A villager at the end of his rope sulks or shouts at his rival for an hour, then is calmer for a day.
source: LIVING_WORLD_RESEARCH #29; RimWorld mental breaks; CK3 stress

description: A villager's fear (the dark, deep water, a beast) gives a bad thought when it happens.
notes: The fear itself is built (Personality.cs); only the bad thought is missing.

description: Mood counts lasting factors with weights (safety 4, food 3, housing 3, social 2, work 2, health 2, sleep 1.5).
A night in a bed lifts the mood more after nights without one.
Every villager eats from the chest each day, and hunger slows or stops work.
notes: Idea only from VikingColonies (licence forbids code). Now villagers only eat when hurt.

feature: Sickness that spreads and a healer
description: Villagers can fall ill, pass it on, and a healer cures them with items from the chest.
source: MineColonies (disease); Banished (nomads bring sickness); Farthest Frontier
notes: A one-off fever event is built (VillageEvents.cs).

description: Villagers need a well nearby or they get sick more often.
Villagers need warm clothes or a fire in winter or they get cold.

feature: Wounded rest in bed and are tended
description: A badly hurt villager lies in bed while a carer brings food.

feature: Cairn or grave for the dead
description: A villager who dies leaves a cairn or grave in the village.
notes: Idea only; VikingColonies code may not be copied or published.

description: Villagers who work too long without rest get worn down and work worse.
Each kind of villager (Viking, Fuling, Dvergr) wants different foods and comforts.
notes: Needs cultures per biome first.

feature: High mood earns the village standing
description: A village whose people stay very happy gains standing with its neighbours over time.
Villagers walk, stop and turn without twitching, sliding or circling their target.
source: ROADMAP M2; LEARNINGS.md; Walker.cs; 2026-11-06 notes S10 to S12
notes: Many fixes built (steady goals, turn angle 90, one rotation driver); jitter still seen in the last test. Trace again with vh trace.

description: A stuck villager steps aside or steps out of a building that trapped him, then tries again.
Villagers use doors on their way and close them behind them.

feature: Villagers pass through players and each other
description: Villagers walk through players and each other.

feature: Walk by default, run on errands
description: Villagers walk around the village and only run on harvest trips, to shelter in a fight, or on a hunt.
Villagers keep out of the hearth, fire pits and campfires on every walk, even the last steps.

feature: Seated and sleeping villagers held still
description: Sitting or lying villagers stay pinned to the seat or bed without bobbing.
notes: A bench shake was seen in the test before the attached fix.

description: A setting caps how many villagers a village can hold.
A setting decides how many villagers each building supports.
notes: Beds now decide capacity; this older setting still exists.

description: With no work, villagers sit by the fire, stroll, chat, keep busy at stations and gesture by the village's mood.
notes: Seen running in the 2026-11-06 tests, with jitter; the ROADMAP item is still open.

description: Villagers sit on the village's benches and chairs, and take a free seat near the hearth in the evening.
notes: Tested: a villager shook on a bench; the attached fix is untested.

description: The first settler still living is the Jarl, who greets strangers first and speaks at gatherings.
The village keeps a small shrine where villagers leave offerings and pray.
source: RimWorld (Ideology); Kingdoms and Castles; Manor Lords; Medieval Dynasty

description: Villagers also need to pray, be creative, make merry or be with friends, and feel it when they cannot.
Sad villagers go to the longhouse and happy ones laugh and dance in the open.
Villagers greet you and say a line when you come near.
About 3,000 lines in eight voices (steady, gruff, cheerful, worrier, wry, elder, young, devout) with conditions on the moment.
notes: Keep growing it (ROADMAP).

description: Lines live in text files inside the logic DLL and reload while the game runs.
A village says at most one unprompted line every 30 to 60 seconds.

feature: Event reactions from two or three villagers
description: A finished building, a newcomer or a fight gets two or three reactions, each a different line.

feature: No repeats until a dozen others
description: A villager does not say the same line again until he has said a dozen others.

feature: Talk about work, wants and needs
description: Lines about what a villager is doing, what he wants and what the village needs.

feature: Villagers stop turning to stare at you
description: Villagers keep facing their work while a player stands near.
notes: This was a main jitter cause in the traces.

description: The nearest willing villager greets a new player; a known player is welcomed back.
Villagers who overhear a line turn to the speaker and answer with a gesture or a spoken reply by its tone.
Two idle villagers meet and trade a short exchange of lines.
A third villager nearby may chime in, and answers come in the answerer's own voice and state.
source: WORLD_LIFE minds; FreeTime.cs; Dialogue.cs; Kenshi; Skyrim scenes

description: Chats depend on who talks: friends, rivals, sweethearts, same trade, a child, the Jarl.
Villagers talk about recent events in the village for a while.
The village remembers each player's visits, gifts, building, kills, deaths, fights, requests done and villagers hit.
notes: Open question from 2026-11-08: hitting a villager costs 2 reputation and killing one 15; Tyler to confirm.

description: Villagers who saw a deed tell others in their chats, so the story spreads through the village.
source: WORLD_LIFE minds; PlayerMemory.cs; Minecraft gossip; Gothic news

description: Lines on a topic you heard a lot lately come up less often for you.
What topics you heard is saved, so a reload does not reset it.
Villagers talk about where they are: the forge, the fire, the chest, the shore, the edge of the village, indoors.
Villagers at a dock get their own lines once villages have docks.
notes: Needs harbour designs in villages.

feature: Weather and time of day lines
description: Villagers talk about rain, storm, snow, mist, dawn, dusk and late night.
Villagers remark on your gear, wounds, wet clothes, heavy pack, boss trophies and skills.
source: WORLD_LIFE minds; Context.cs; player.txt; Skyrim barks

description: Villagers remark when the weather turns, at dawn and dusk, when a boss falls, when you draw a weapon or sneak, and when beasts come near.
Standing villagers glance at a neighbour, at you, at an animal, at the sky in rain, or warm their hands at the fire.
Each villager has a homeland, a favourite food, a fear, a pastime and a hope he talks about.
Each villager has a friend and a rival in the village who shape his chats and mood.
Villagers remember what they did yesterday and village events for two to five days.
A villager wants one thing at a time (a bed, a bigger house, a skill, a feast, news, a hunt) and is pleased when it comes true.
Two friends who chat often become sweethearts, written in the chronicle.
A villager may want to make peace with his rival and does so after a few chats.

feature: Newcomers tell why they left home
description: A newcomer tells for three days why he left his old home.
An idle villager walks over to watch a neighbour build, fell, cook or mine, or a visitor, and comments.
Wave or cheer and up to three villagers nearby answer in kind.

feature: A villager sits with you by the fire
description: Sit by the village fire and a villager comes to sit and talk for a while.

feature: A meal for a hurt player
description: A badly hurt player in the village by day is brought a cooked meal from the chest.
A player who walks in late at night gets a remark.
Elders tell stories from the older half of the chronicle.

feature: Hover text with task and reason
description: Looking at a villager shows his name, what he is doing, why he has no work, and his mood.
source: 2026-11-05 note S5; VillagerBehaviour.cs; 2026-11-05 note S7 test

description: Each villager follows a day plan of blocks (sleep, eat, work, chores, free, social) with places, so friends meet at the same spot.
source: LIVING_WORLD_RESEARCH #14; Gothic; Ultima VII; Stardew Valley

feature: Free time chosen by what places offer
description: Tired villagers find a bench, cold ones the fire, lonely ones a crowd; new seats get used.
Rude talk can lower opinion and sometimes start a fist fight between two villagers.
notes: A quarrel event between rivals is built (VillageEvents.cs).

description: A big event can slowly change a villager's character over many days.
Each villager has a friendship level with you that rises with talk and gifts and opens special scenes.
Each villager loves, likes or hates certain gifts, and repeated gifts count for less.
source: LIVING_WORLD_RESEARCH (Stardew gift values, MCA gift fatigue)
notes: Gifts of materials to the chest are already counted.

description: Villagers have birthdays when gifts count for more.
Villagers you know leave you a short letter or note now and then.
notes: Needs a place for letters (a sign, a chest).

feature: A villager says he will move away
description: A villager announces days ahead that he plans to leave, so you can change his mind.

feature: Bystanders gather to watch a fight
description: Villagers come to watch when someone fights nearby.
A villager who sees you take from the chest without putting in remembers it and tells others.

feature: Villagers give hints about the world
description: Any villager can point you to a place worth finding, the way hermits do.
notes: Hermits already pin places (WorldLife.cs).

feature: Values and approval of your choices
description: Villagers approve or object to what you did by their own character.
Talking to a villager opens a short tree of questions and answers that depend on quests, standing and time.
source: CustomNPC+; ServerGuide; Marketplace NPCs; Norse Personality Construction System

description: Special short scenes play when your friendship with a villager reaches set levels.
Children chase each other and play tag round the village.
source: Minecraft (babies play tag); Ultima VII (kid games)

description: Villagers fell trees and break rocks for the village's wood and stone.
The village counts wood, fine wood, core wood and stone, priced from vanilla recipes.
Material on the ground first, then felled logs and cracked rocks, then fresh trees and rocks; loose sticks and stones only when nothing bigger is near.
notes: This is a CLAUDE.md project rule.

feature: Nobody harvests when nothing is needed
description: Villagers stop gathering when the village needs nothing.
notes: This is a CLAUDE.md project rule.

feature: Pick trees by the wood they give
description: A villager who needs core wood goes for a pine; one who needs fine wood goes for a birch or oak.
Hammer to build, axe for trees, pickaxe for rocks, hoe for paths.
Reach is checked against the real surface before every blow.

feature: Stand spots for trees, logs and rocks
description: A villager walks to a spot beside the target, faces it and swings from a standstill.

feature: Trees felled away from the village
description: Trees are cut from the hearth side so they fall away from the buildings.
source: ROADMAP M2; LEARNINGS.md; Vikings for Hire
notes: Built 2026-11-05 S2; the ROADMAP item is still open.

description: Two villagers never work the same tree or rock.
Villagers chop and mine about as fast as a player does.
A new village gathers from nothing for its first building; there is no free starting stock.
A village unloaded while you were away catches up on growth and earns some wood when you return.
One villager is the builder; he builds whenever the chest covers the next piece and gathers otherwise.
The builder stands right by each piece and taps it with the hammer's own animation.

feature: Pieces only go up while the builder is there
description: A piece appears only while the builder stands next to it.
A builder or path layer who has to fight stops, then picks up where he left off.

feature: Builder waits when someone is in the way
description: The builder waits while a player or villager stands where the next piece goes.
A builder who misses a spot twice waits, then places from where he stands.

feature: Each piece takes a few taps
description: Each piece takes a couple of seconds of hammering before it appears.
Villagers are protectors or carers at random, never by gender; arrivals alternate; roles show in idle time and emergencies.
notes: Tyler decided roles never depend on gender.

description: From six villagers, trades by arrival order (carpenter, woodcutter, miner, cook, farmer); before that everyone works the biggest need.
A trade only sets which work a villager prefers; everyone can harvest, build and defend.
Men and women take different trades, as in Millénaire's Norman villages.
notes: Tyler decided roles and trades never depend on gender (2026-11-05, 2026-11-06).

feature: Builder and crafter roles when the chest is full
description: With enough in the chest nobody harvests; villagers switch to building and crafting or furnishing.
With little food in the chest, a protector hunts boar, deer or hare near the village and brings the meat home.
A carer picks berries and mushrooms near the village when food is low.

feature: Farms with berry and mushroom rows
description: Farmers plant raspberry bushes and mushrooms (blueberries in the Black Forest) in rows behind a farm and harvest them.
A farmer tends and harvests the farms and keeps the chest in food.
Farms grow crops from seeds, such as carrots in the Black Forest.
notes: Crops need cultivated ground (BLUEPRINT_LAB limits).

description: A carer tends the hearth each morning.
Idle villagers make a cooking station and benches by the hearth from what the chest can spare.
The carpenter or builder crafts each gear tier's set at the recipe's real station from chest materials.
notes: On by default (SmithMakesGear). Existing villages keep their tier.

description: The village builds its own forge so it can make bronze gear at home.
Made gear goes into the chest and each villager takes his weapon, tool and armour from it.
source: WORLD_LIFE Next 7; Hearth and Village (armoury chest); Millénaire (fetch a tool)
notes: Check against the one-chest rule in CLAUDE.md if gear needs its own chest.

description: Worn tools and weapons are repaired at a station that can repair them.
source: WORLD_LIFE Next 7; Offline Companions Reborn (MIT); Guard Villagers

description: Nine skills that rise with work and make felling, mining and building faster.
source: WORLD_LIFE minds; VillagerSkills.cs; MineColonies; Medieval Dynasty

description: A villager who watches a neighbour work learns a little of that skill.
A happy villager now and then works faster for a while.
notes: Built, then removed by D-014 (2026-11-08): mood plays no part in work speed (Villagers/Chores.cs, Villagers/VillagerSkills.cs).

description: A happy village builds faster and a glum one slower (0.85 to 1.3 times).
source: 2026-11-06 note S2; ROADMAP Later ideas; Millénaire; Hirdmandr
notes: Built, then removed by D-014 (2026-11-08): mood plays no part in work speed (Villagers/Chores.cs, Villagers/VillagerSkills.cs).

feature: Skill cap from the home's level
description: A villager's skill cannot pass a cap set by his house's level.

feature: Children start from their parents' skills
description: A child's starting skills come from his parents.
A skilled villager gets more wood or stone from each tree or rock.
Trades go to the villagers best at that work.
Each villager is born better at some work and worse at other work, and gets the work he is good at.

feature: A trade appears when its station exists
description: A forge brings a smith, a loom a weaver, a kiln a charcoal burner.
Work buildings with their stations stand near the trees, rocks or water they use.
notes: Workshops near trees and rocks built; more profession buildings to come.

feature: Builders carry materials to the site
description: The builder visibly carries each load from the chest to the site.
source: ROADMAP Later ideas; LEARNINGS.md; Village Masters

feature: Builder takes the whole bill at once
description: The builder takes the full cost of a building from the chest in one trip.
notes: Tyler's decision 2026-11-06: materials are paid per piece.

description: Villagers run a kiln and a smelter to turn wood and ore into coal and metal.
A villager fishes from the shore or a dock for food.
One villager keeps every fire and torch in the village fuelled.
A villager sorts what is brought in into the right chests.
source: Vikings for Hire; Fuling Workforce; Hearthfolk
notes: Only matters if the village has more than one chest; see the one-chest rule in CLAUDE.md.

description: A villager brews mead at a cauldron and fermenter.
A villager keeps bee hives for honey.
notes: Fits: crafted bee hives (piece_beehive, from a queen bee) are a normal piece. Only wild hives are kept out (Tyler, 2026-11-08).

description: A storehouse with couriers who carry goods between buildings and the store.
notes: Conflicts with the one-chest rule in CLAUDE.md unless Tyler widens it.

description: A worker who lacks an item asks for it, and a crafter who knows the recipe makes it and its inputs.
A better axe or pickaxe makes a villager work faster.
notes: Tool tier already decides what a villager can break.

feature: Work areas set by the player
description: You mark an area where a worker cuts or mines.
notes: Villheim villages run themselves; this adds player direction.

description: How many villagers can work at once depends on the village's level.
Fields lose quality if the same crop grows too long and need rotating.
Fields and stores can be hit by blight or rats.
Each part of a large village keeps its own stock and haulers move goods between them.

feature: Ask a villager to help you
description: Ask a villager to gather logs or help on your own build for a while.

feature: A masterwork in a strange mood
description: Now and then a villager is struck by a mood, takes over a station and makes one fine item.
notes: Must be a vanilla item; no new assets.

description: Buildings are copied from locations in the game and installed mods at runtime.
notes: CLAUDE.md: existing designs and assets only.

feature: More World Locations as a source
description: Houses, taverns, barns, forges and towers from More World Locations are used when it is installed.
notes: Read from Tyler's install only (All Rights Reserved).

description: Random ruin damage is off and loot, spawners and creatures are left out, so copied houses look lived in.

feature: Copy a location's own terrain shaping
description: A copied building's ground is levelled the way the original location levels it.
notes: Replaced 2026-11-06 S12 by flat pads at floor height for village buildings.

description: A building goes up in stages: structure, roof, doors and windows, interior.
Ground up, every piece held when placed; doors and windows before what rests on them.
source: ROADMAP M2; CLAUDE.md rule; BuildOrder.cs; Innangard
notes: CLAUDE.md building-order rule.

description: Wild bee hives, which poison villagers and players nearby, are left out of designs; crafted bee hives are copied like any piece.
notes: Rule narrowed 2026-11-08 (Tyler): crafted bee hives are fine. Untested in game.

description: A setting lists objects never copied from designs.
A village only builds designs whose materials exist in its biome (no core wood in the Meadows).
notes: Known issue: it drops Meadows MWL designs that use core wood, likely the Meadows tavern.

feature: Outpost materials count for the biome rule
description: A village may build with what its outposts send home, so a Meadows village with a forest camp can use core wood.
notes: Tyler decided this 2026-11-08.

feature: Caravan cargo counts for the biome rule
description: Goods brought by trade caravans would also count toward what a village can build.
notes: Open question for Tyler. Today only outposts count.

feature: Stone building waits until the village advances
description: Meadows villages build in wood and only use stone once they reach a later stage.
notes: Still to decide.

description: Villages can build from .blueprint and .vbuild files in Villheim's and PlanBuild's folders.
notes: No finished village blueprints are in the folder yet.

description: Blueprints named role-family-level form upgrade chains (house-cabin-1, house-cabin-2).
Blueprints under an inspiration folder show in the gallery and PlanBuild; villages skip them.
Other creators' blueprints are read from Tyler's install and never committed or shipped.
The OverDrive BiomeBlueprints pack used as a design source.
notes: Blacklisted by Tyler 2026-11-08. Open: whether the 12 other-creator builds in Keepers.cs stay.

feature: Growth tiers and one pending project
description: What to build next follows tiers, weighted picks and one pending project, as in Millénaire.
Homes until every villager has a bed, then the longhouse, then the hub and a workshop and storehouse, then more homes, farms and workshops.
Essentials (cooking station, beds) come before any new building; comfort pieces follow.
A longhouse with a fire pit is placed so its fire sits on the village hearth.
A small storehouse with extra chests goes up early.
notes: Check against the one-chest rule in CLAUDE.md.

description: A building is swapped for a better design of the same role; the old one comes down roof first with half the materials back.
notes: Tyler decided upgrades refund half (2026-11-06).

description: Interiors grow with the village: bed and chest, then chairs and a table, then more.
Beds and workbenches go only where the game's cover test passes, so stations work.
Beds that came with a design count for the village even if nobody built them.
The builder puts back broken pieces, structural first and cosmetic later, levelling the ground under ground pieces.
Villagers fill a gap in a row or a missing course when no saved design covers the piece.
A house left empty for ten days stops being repaired and starts to wear.
One chest by the hearth holds the building materials; villagers and players fill it and the builder builds from it.
source: ROADMAP M2; CLAUDE.md rule; VillageChest.cs; 2026-11-06 note S10
notes: Seen working in the 2026-11-06 S10 test; the ROADMAP item is still open. CLAUDE.md rule.

description: If the village chest is destroyed, rebuilding it comes before anything else.
A notice board from Tyler's villagenotice blueprint stands over the village chest.
source: ROADMAP M2; NoticeBoard.cs; 2026-11-06 notes S13, S14
notes: Not built in the 2026-11-06 S14 test; the payment fix is untested.

description: Extra chests appear under the notice board as the village grows.
notes: Check against the one-chest rule in CLAUDE.md.

description: The notice board moves inside the longhouse once there is one.
The storehouse chests move into the central hall when the hall is rebuilt bigger.
notes: Tyler 2026-11-10: "Two entirely different buildings. One is a work building (storage) and the other a social hub." Not to be built.

feature: Building ground flat at floor height
description: Each building stands on a flat pad at its ground floor's height, with bare earth and a slope out.
source: ROADMAP M2; ConstructionSite.cs; 2026-11-06 notes S12, S13
notes: vh buildingground tested; village pads untested.

description: Hillside designs sit so most of their foundation stands on the ground.
Every site is flattened before the first piece and under each ground piece as it goes up.
Designs that trap villagers (low beams, blocked doors) are left out.

feature: Curated Meadows and Black Forest sets
description: Tyler's hand-picked blueprint sets with upgrade levels for the Meadows and Black Forest.
notes: Slotting under way: Meadows hearth first.

description: Villages pick a base ID per kind and biome and build s1 at d1, raising d and s over time.
The reader understands <baseID>_s#d# names and the sheet's type, subtype and biome.
Between upgrades villagers add the pieces d2 has and d1 lacks one at a time; a new s# is a real rebuild.
Villages build a save's paths, paving and levelled spots along with its pieces.
notes: Read board saves with FromFile(asSaved: true).

feature: Ship Tyler's blueprints with the mod
description: Finished blueprints come inside the mod so PlanBuild is only needed to make them.
notes: Licensing: ship only Tyler's own builds or builds with the creator's permission.

description: Villages may build designs the blueprint lab generated, once Tyler marks them Yes.
notes: Conflicts with CLAUDE.md 'existing designs and assets only'. Tyler approved in principle; wording for CLAUDE.md still to agree.

description: Water wheels, outhouses and gardens built in idle time to make the village look lived in.
The hearth grows from a campfire to a hearth with the cooking station, then larger vanilla fire pieces.
notes: Needs a core change (game restart).

feature: Ghost preview of the next building
description: A see-through preview shows where the next building will stand.
A village that likes you enough builds you a house.

feature: Rooms by what is in them
description: A building's use comes from its furniture (bed and light: home; forge: smithy) and missing pieces are added.
source: LIVING_WORLD_RESEARCH #20; Dragon Quest Builders 2; Starbound; Terraria

description: Rooms get a grade from size and furnishing that affects mood.
You mark a plot or pick a design and the village builds it from its chest.
source: Dragon Quest Builders 2; MineColonies; Sim Settlements 2
notes: Villheim villages choose for themselves today.

description: A building gets an attached part later, such as a guest room on the hall.
Each design type has a cap on how many a village may have.
A big village builds one special landmark.
Walking paths are worked out again after a building goes up so villagers find the new doors.
Villagers find their way up stairs and through rooms with their own map of each building.
A village's look comes from a style set that can be swapped.
notes: Close to cultures by biome (ROADMAP M5).

description: Players share buildings as files that villages can use.
Buildings weather over time and need upkeep.
The world generator places village sites (a single hearth) in the Meadows and Black Forest.
A site becomes a village with a name, a first building and settlers when a player first comes near.
Each village gets a name.
All village data is stored on the hearth so it saves with the world.
Only some sites become villages, at least 1,500 m apart and 400 m from traders and ports.
Settings for how many villages, which biomes, distance between them and from spawn.
The ground round a new hearth is cleared and made flat.
A village only grows while a player is near and catches up on return.
Buildings sit on a grid lined up with the village axis.
